sentences.en: Good morning, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家早上好。

sentences.en: Today we’ll continue our discussion on the art of speaking, focusing on the use of metaphors in speaking.
sentences.zh: 今天我们继续讨论说话的艺术，重点谈谈说话时隐喻的运用。

sentences.en: Now, why do we need to talk about metaphors in speaking?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们为什么需要讨论说话时的隐喻呢？

sentences.en: Well, according to research findings, we utter about six metaphors a minute.
sentences.zh: 研究发现，我们平均每分钟会说出大约六个隐喻。

sentences.en: And metaphorical thinking is essential to how we understand ourselves and others, how we communicate, learn, discover and invent.
sentences.zh: 隐喻思维对于我们理解自己和他人，以及交流、学习、发现和发明，都至关重要。

sentences.en: Actually, metaphor is a way of thought before it is a way with words.
sentences.zh: 实际上，隐喻首先是一种思维方式，然后才是一种语言表达方式。

sentences.en: Now, to assist me in explaining this, I've enlisted the help of a man whose contributions to the field are so tremendous that he himself has become a metaphor.
sentences.zh: 为了帮助解释这一点，我请来了一位男士助阵；他对这个领域的贡献如此巨大，以至于他本人都已成为一个隐喻。

sentences.en: I am, of course, referring to none other than Elvis Presley.
sentences.zh: 当然，我说的正是“猫王”埃尔维斯·普雷斯利。

sentences.en: His All Shook Up is such a touching love song.
sentences.zh: 他的《All Shook Up》是一首十分动人的情歌。

sentences.en: It’s also an example of how we inevitably resort to metaphor when we deal with anything abstract, like ideas, emotions, feelings, concepts, thoughts.
sentences.zh: 这首歌也说明，当我们处理观念、情绪、感受、概念和思想等抽象事物时，总会不可避免地借助隐喻。

sentences.en: In this, Elvis is following Aristotle’s classic definition of metaphor, that is, metaphor is the process of giving the thing a name that belongs to something else.
sentences.zh: 在这里，猫王遵循了亚里士多德对隐喻的经典定义：隐喻，就是把原本属于其他事物的名称赋予某个事物的过程。

sentences.en: And this is the mathematics of metaphor.
sentences.zh: 这就是隐喻的数学表达。

sentences.en: X equals Y.
sentences.zh: X等于Y。

sentences.en: It’s very simple, isn’t it?
sentences.zh: 很简单，对不对？

sentences.en: This formula works wherever metaphor is present.
sentences.zh: 只要存在隐喻，这个公式就适用。

sentences.en: Elvis used metaphor, and so does Shakespeare in this famous line from Romeo and Juliet, that is, “Juliet is the sun.”
sentences.zh: 猫王运用了隐喻，莎士比亚在《罗密欧与朱丽叶》的这句名言中也运用了隐喻：“朱丽叶就是太阳。”

sentences.en: Now here, Shakespeare gives the thing, Juliet, a name that belongs to something else, the sun.
sentences.zh: 这里，莎士比亚给朱丽叶这个人物赋予了一个属于另一事物的名称——太阳。

sentences.en: In fact, whenever we give a thing a name that belongs to something else, we give it a whole network of analogies too.
sentences.zh: 实际上，每当我们用另一个事物的名称来称呼某个事物时，也为它赋予了一整套类比关系。

sentences.en: We mix and match what we know about the metaphor’s source, in this case, the sun, with what we know about its target, Juliet.
sentences.zh: 我们把自己对隐喻源域的认识——这里是对太阳的认识，与对目标域朱丽叶的认识，进行组合搭配。

sentences.en: And metaphor gives us a much more vivid understanding of Juliet than if Shakespeare had literally described just what she looks like.
sentences.zh: 相比莎士比亚直接描述朱丽叶的外貌，隐喻让我们对她产生了更加生动的认识。

sentences.en: So how do we make and interpret metaphors?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们是怎样创造和理解隐喻的呢？

sentences.en: This might look familiar.
sentences.zh: 这可能听起来很熟悉。

sentences.en: The first step is pattern recognition.
sentences.zh: 第一步是模式识别。

sentences.en: Metaphor is not just the detection of patterns; instead, it is the creation of patterns.
sentences.zh: 隐喻不只是识别模式，更是在创造模式。

sentences.en: And the second step is conceptual synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 第二步是概念联觉。

sentences.en: And what is synesthesia?
sentences.zh: 什么是联觉呢？

sentences.en: It is the experience of a stimulus received by one sense organ and another sense organ as well, for example, like colored hearing.
sentences.zh: 联觉是这样一种体验：原本由某一感觉器官接收的刺激，同时也被另一个感觉器官感知，例如色听联觉。

sentences.en: People with colored hearing actually see colors when they hear the sounds of words or letters.
sentences.zh: 有色听联觉的人，在听到单词或字母的声音时，真的会看到颜色。

sentences.en: We all have synesthetic abilities, and many of the metaphors we use every day are synesthetic.
sentences.zh: 我们都具有联觉能力，而日常使用的许多隐喻都具有联觉性质。

sentences.en: For instance, silence is sweet.
sentences.zh: 比如，宁静是甜美的。

w.m: adj. 甜美的；令人愉悦的

sentences.en: Neckties are loud.
sentences.zh: 领带是“响亮”的，也就是花哨醒目的。

w.m: adj. 花哨醒目的（借用响亮之义）

sentences.en: So metaphor creates a kind of conceptual synesthesia, in which we understand one concept in the context of another.
sentences.zh: 所以，隐喻创造了一种概念联觉，让我们借助另一个概念的背景来理解一个概念。

sentences.en: Let’s move on to the third step, that is cognitive dissonance.
sentences.zh: 接着看第三步，也就是认知失调。

sentences.en: There is a test called the Stroop test.
sentences.zh: 有一种测试叫斯特鲁普测试。

sentences.en: What you need to do is identify as quickly as possible the color of the ink in which words of color are printed.
sentences.zh: 你需要尽快辨认出印刷颜色词时所用墨水的颜色。

sentences.en: If you’re like most people, you’ll experience a moment of cognitive dissonance when the name of the color is printed in a differently colored ink.
sentences.zh: 如果你和大多数人一样，当颜色名称用另一种颜色的墨水印出来时，会经历片刻的认知失调。

sentences.en: For example, the word “red” is printed in blue ink.
sentences.zh: 比如，“红”这个字用蓝色墨水印出来。

sentences.en: Then you may wonder what the test intends to tell us.
sentences.zh: 你可能会想，这个测试究竟要告诉我们什么。

sentences.en: Well, the test shows that we cannot overlook the literal meaning of words, even when the literal meaning gives the wrong answer.
sentences.zh: 这个测试表明，我们无法忽略词语的字面意义，即使它会导向错误答案。

sentences.en: Stroop tests have been done with metaphor as well.
sentences.zh: 研究人员也用隐喻做过斯特鲁普测试。

sentences.en: The participants had to identify as quickly as possible the literally false sentences.
sentences.zh: 参与者必须尽可能快地找出字面意义上不成立的句子。

sentences.en: They took longer to reject metaphors as false than they did to reject literally false sentences.
sentences.zh: 相比其他字面意义上不成立的句子，他们需要更长时间，才能把隐喻句判定为错误。

sentences.en: Why? Because we cannot ignore the metaphorical meaning of words either.
sentences.zh: 为什么？因为我们同样无法忽视词语的隐喻意义。

sentences.en: For example, one of the sentences was, “Some jobs are jails.”
sentences.zh: 比如，其中一句是：“有些工作就是监狱。”

sentences.en: Now, unless you’re a prison guard yourself, the sentence “Some jobs are jails.” is literally false.
sentences.zh: 除非你自己就是狱警，否则“有些工作就是监狱”这句话，从字面上说是不成立的。

sentences.en: Sadly, it’s metaphorically true.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，从隐喻意义上说，它却是真的。

sentences.en: And the metaphorical truth interferes with our ability to identify it as literally false.
sentences.zh: 这种隐喻层面的真实，会干扰我们把它判为字面意义上不成立的句子。

sentences.en: Metaphor matters because it’s around us every day, all the time.
sentences.zh: 隐喻之所以重要，是因为它每天、时时刻刻都在我们身边。

sentences.en: How and in what ways does metaphor matter?
sentences.zh: 隐喻究竟是怎样、又在哪些方面发挥作用的？

sentences.en: Well, I’d say metaphor matters, first of all, because it creates expectations.
sentences.zh: 首先，我认为隐喻很重要，因为它能塑造预期。

sentences.en: So pay careful attention the next time you read some financial news.
sentences.zh: 所以，下次阅读财经新闻时，请格外留心。

sentences.en: Agent metaphors describe price movements as the deliberate action of a living thing, as in, “The NASDAQ climbed higher.”
sentences.zh: 施事隐喻把价格变动描述成生命体有意为之的动作，比如：“纳斯达克指数继续向上攀爬。”

sentences.en: Object metaphors describe price movements as non-living things, as in, “The Dow fell like a brick.”
sentences.zh: 物体隐喻则把价格变动描述为无生命物体的运动，比如：“道琼斯指数像砖块一样坠落。”

sentences.en: Researchers once asked a group of people to read market commentaries and then predict the next day’s price trend.
sentences.zh: 研究人员曾让一组人阅读市场评论，再预测第二天的价格走势。

sentences.en: Those exposed to agent metaphors had higher expectations that price trends would continue.
sentences.zh: 接触施事隐喻的人，更倾向于预期价格走势会持续下去。

sentences.en: And they had those expectations because agent metaphors imply the deliberate action of a living thing pursuing a goal.
sentences.zh: 他们之所以这样预期，是因为施事隐喻暗示：某个生命体正在有意识地采取行动，追求一个目标。

sentences.en: If, for example, house prices are routinely described as climbing and climbing, higher and higher, people might naturally assume that rise is incessant.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果房价经常被描述为不断攀升、越爬越高，人们自然可能以为上涨会永不停息。

w.m: adj. 不停的；持续不断的

sentences.en: Also, metaphor matters because it influences decisions by activating analogies.
sentences.zh: 隐喻也很重要，因为它能激活类比，从而影响决策。

sentences.en: Let me give you an example, which was actually an experiment.
sentences.zh: 我来举个例子，这实际上是一项实验。

sentences.en: A group of students was told that a small country had been invaded and had asked for help.
sentences.zh: 一组学生被告知：有个小国遭到入侵，并请求援助。

sentences.en: And they had to make a decision.
sentences.zh: 他们必须作出决定。

sentences.en: What should they do? Intervene, appeal to the United Nations, or just do nothing?
sentences.zh: 他们该怎么办呢？进行干预、向联合国求助，还是袖手旁观？

sentences.en: They were each then given one of the three descriptions of this hypothetical crisis.
sentences.zh: 随后，每名学生都收到了关于这一假设危机的三种描述之一。

sentences.en: Each of the three descriptions was designed to trigger a different historical analogy: World War II, Vietnam, and the third was historically neutral.
sentences.zh: 这三种描述分别旨在唤起不同的历史类比：第二次世界大战、越南战争，以及第三种不带历史指向的描述。

w.m: adj. 中立的；不带倾向的

sentences.en: Those exposed to the World War II scenario made more interventionist recommendations than the others.
sentences.zh: 接触到二战情境描述的人，提出了比其他人更多的干预主义建议。

sentences.en: This shows that just as we cannot ignore the literal meaning of words, we cannot ignore the analogies that are triggered by metaphor.
sentences.zh: 这说明，正如我们无法忽略词语的字面意义一样，也无法忽略隐喻所引发的类比。

sentences.en: Metaphor matters because it opens the door to discovery.
sentences.zh: 隐喻很重要，因为它为新发现打开了大门。

sentences.en: Whenever we solve a problem or make a discovery, we compare what we know with what we don’t know.
sentences.zh: 每当解决问题或有所发现时，我们都在比较已知与未知。

sentences.en: And the only way to find out about the latter is to investigate the ways it might be like the former.
sentences.zh: 要了解后者，唯一的办法就是探究它可能在哪些方面与前者相似。

sentences.en: Now, we know that metaphor is ubiquitous, yet it’s hidden.
sentences.zh: 现在我们知道，隐喻无处不在，却又隐藏着。

sentences.en: But you just have to look at the words around you, and you'll find it.
sentences.zh: 但只要看看周围的词语，你就会发现它。

sentences.en: Ralph Waldo Emerson described language as “fossil poetry.”
sentences.zh: 拉尔夫·沃尔多·爱默生把语言描述为“化石般的诗”。

w.m: n. 化石般的诗（比喻凝固于语言的诗意）

sentences.en: But before, it was fossil metaphor, and these fossils still breathe.
sentences.zh: 但在此之前，它是化石般的隐喻，而这些化石至今仍在呼吸。

sentences.en: OK, let me sum up today’s lecture.
sentences.zh: 好，让我总结一下今天的讲座。

sentences.en: We’ve looked at how metaphor is defined, how people understand metaphors, and how metaphors might influence people’s expectations and decisions.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论了隐喻的定义、人们如何理解隐喻，以及隐喻可能怎样影响人的预期和决策。

sentences.en: Before we call it a day, I'd like to walk you through a famous quote from Francis Bacon: “Some books are to be tasted, others swallowed, and some few to be chewed and digested.”
sentences.zh: 结束之前，我想带大家细读弗朗西斯·培根的一句名言：“书有可浅尝者，有可吞食者，少数则须咀嚼消化。”

w.m: phr. 带领某人逐步了解

sentences.en: Well, how many metaphors are there in the statement?
sentences.zh: 那么，这句话里有多少个隐喻呢？

sentences.en: That’s your takeaway homework.
sentences.zh: 这就是留给大家的课后作业。

w.m: n. 课后带走完成的作业

待核: 原PDF第2页确印“But before, it was fossil metaphor”；before所指及实际措辞须听原声核实，目前未擅改。

sentences.en: Good evening, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家晚上好。

sentences.en: Today, we are delighted to have invited Jim Johnson, a gapyear.com’s spokesperson, to talk about gap year.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们很高兴邀请到gapyear.com网站的发言人吉姆·约翰逊，来谈谈间隔年。

sentences.en: So, whether you’re currently deciding whether a gap year is for you, or you’re just feeling itchy to decide what to do with it, you are welcome to join us. Well, Jim.
sentences.zh: 无论你正在考虑自己是否适合间隔年，还是已经迫不及待地想决定如何度过间隔年，都欢迎加入我们。那么，吉姆。

w.m: adj. 跃跃欲试的；急切的

sentences.en: Thanks. I am very pleased to meet you all.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。很高兴见到大家。

sentences.en: Now, let me first ask you a question. Why should young people be thinking seriously about taking a gap year?
sentences.zh: 我先问您一个问题。为什么年轻人应该认真考虑过一个间隔年呢？

sentences.en: Well, I get asked this question all the time.
sentences.zh: 我一直都会被问到这个问题。

sentences.en: People will tell you that a gap year boosts your CV, that it makes you more employable, or that it even prepares you for a life at university.
sentences.zh: 别人会告诉你，间隔年能为简历加分，让你更容易就业，甚至能帮助你为大学生活做好准备。

sentences.en: Well, this is the case, but I find not enough people put an emphasis on just how amazing a gap year really is.
sentences.zh: 这些话确实没错，但我发现，还没有足够多的人强调间隔年本身有多么精彩。

sentences.en: Eh, it’s a life changing experience, and it’s unbelievable how much fun you can have on a gap year.
sentences.zh: 它能改变人生，而你在间隔年里获得的乐趣之多，也会令人难以置信。

sentences.en: So, what is the best thing about taking a gap year?
sentences.zh: 那么，间隔年最大的好处是什么呢？

sentences.en: I think taking a gap year is like making a journey.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，间隔年就像开启一段旅程。

sentences.en: It’s an education, an exploration and an adventure.
sentences.zh: 它是一次学习、一次探索，也是一场冒险。

sentences.en: You learn so much about exotic cultures and traditions, their culinary art, their political system, their religion.
sentences.zh: 你能深入了解异国文化与传统，以及那里的烹饪艺术、政治制度和宗教。

sentences.en: In each new location, you’re learning more and more, and that ultimately adds more value to yourself, which is the best thing, I think.
sentences.zh: 每到一个新地方，你都会学到越来越多东西，最终让自身更有价值；我觉得，这才是最棒的。

sentences.en: What did your gap year involve?
sentences.zh: 您的间隔年都做了些什么？

sentences.en: I travelled for two years through Central Asia, Southeast Asia and Australia, you know, backpacking, volunteering and moonlighting abroad.
sentences.zh: 我用了两年时间游历中亚、东南亚和澳大利亚，在国外背包旅行、做志愿服务，也打些零工。

sentences.en: So I had a pretty comprehensive gap.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的间隔年经历相当丰富。

sentences.en: To put it simple, it was the best two years in my life.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，那是我人生中最美好的两年。

w.m: 表达. 简单来说（规范表达为to put it simply）

sentences.en: It can be difficult to decide what to do and where to go on your gap year, so what advice would you have for people finding it tricky?
sentences.zh: 决定间隔年做什么、去哪里，可能很困难；对于为此感到棘手的人，您有什么建议？

sentences.en: Good question. The most important thing is research and planning.
sentences.zh: 问得好。最重要的是调研和规划。

sentences.en: That is, sit down with a map and a sheet of paper.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，拿张地图和一张纸，坐下来好好想想。

sentences.en: List where you want to go and why.
sentences.zh: 列出你想去哪里，以及为什么想去。

sentences.en: Maybe even throw in a pros and cons column.
sentences.zh: 甚至还可以加上一栏，写下利弊。

sentences.en: Others may advise talking to friends with some experience of gap year, or browse some online forums, which I personally would not highly recommend.
sentences.zh: 有人可能建议找有间隔年经验的朋友聊聊，或浏览网上论坛；我个人并不特别推荐这些做法。

sentences.en: Don’t choose what is the best out there, but what is most appropriate for you.
sentences.zh: 不要选择外界公认最好的，而要选择最适合自己的。

sentences.en: OK, let’s move on to another question.
sentences.zh: 好，我们接着谈另一个问题。

sentences.en: Which project would you do if you were taking a gap year?
sentences.zh: 如果您要过一个间隔年，您会选择哪个项目？

sentences.en: I’m a bit of a diving nut, so I would go for the Madagascar Marine Conservation and Diving Project.
sentences.zh: 我是个潜水迷，所以会选择马达加斯加海洋保护与潜水项目。

sentences.en: It’s got everything you want.
sentences.zh: 你想要的，它都具备。

sentences.en: It’s relatively cheap, especially when you consider what you’re getting, and you get to learn all about marine conservation.
sentences.zh: 它的费用相对便宜，尤其考虑到你能获得的收获；你还能全面学习海洋保护知识。

sentences.en: Oh, and it’s in Madagascar, one of the best places to go diving in the world.
sentences.zh: 而且，项目在马达加斯加，那可是世界上最适合潜水的地方之一。

sentences.en: Do employers or universities care what you’ve done on your gap year?
sentences.zh: 雇主或大学会在意你在间隔年里做过什么吗？

sentences.en: Yes, they really do. If you’re studying veterinary science and you volunteer on a wildlife conservation project, then that can really boost your CV and experience levels by doing so.
sentences.zh: 会的，他们确实很在意。如果你学兽医学，又参加了野生动物保护项目的志愿工作，这样的经历就能实实在在地为简历加分、丰富你的经验。

sentences.en: Recently, at gapyear.com, we conducted a survey asking HR professionals whether a gap year makes a job applicant more employable. 63% agreed that a constructive gap year, either just a few months or a year sharp spent volunteering or gaining work experience overseas, makes a job application stand out, so the evidence is there.
sentences.zh: 最近，gapyear.com对人力资源专业人士开展了一项调查，询问间隔年是否会让求职者更具就业竞争力。63%的受访者表示，一段有意义的间隔年经历，无论是几个月还是一年，用来参加志愿活动或积累海外工作经验，都能使求职申请脱颖而出；这就是依据。

w.m: adj. 有益的；有建设性的

sentences.en: What is part one of the interview mainly about?
sentences.zh: 这次访谈的第一部分主要谈什么？

sentences.en: According to the man, why should young people think seriously about taking a gap year?
sentences.zh: 根据这位男士的说法，年轻人为什么应该认真考虑过间隔年？

sentences.en: What does the man say about the best thing of taking a gap year?
sentences.zh: 这位男士认为，间隔年最大的好处是什么？

sentences.en: What is the man’s advice for young people before they start a gap year?
sentences.zh: 对于即将开始间隔年的年轻人，这位男士有什么建议？

sentences.en: According to the man, what kind of gap year experience do employers care most?
sentences.zh: 根据这位男士的说法，雇主最看重哪类间隔年经历？

待核: 原PDF第3页确印“a year sharp spent volunteering”；sharp为扫描原稿本身疑误，须原声裁决，英文暂保留，不给sharp强加词义。
原PDF第3页确印“To put it simple”；尚待原声核对simple/simply，未擅自改口语措辞。
第5题扫描题干为“what kind of gap year experience do employers care most?”，缺about；待核实际口述，暂按原扫描保留。

units.title: Part Two of the Interview

source_refs.original_pdf: B1专八历年真题+听力+解析/01.历年真题+解析/2023年专八真题+音频+解析/2023年英语专八真题解析.pdf
source_refs.verified_against: 原PDF页图逐篇查看；正文及B部末尾题干，未混入参考答案或解题说明

sentences.en: Now, Jim, you said a gap year can be just a few months?
sentences.zh: 吉姆，您刚才说，间隔年也可以只有几个月？

sentences.en: So what if people don’t want to take a whole year out?
sentences.zh: 那如果有人不想拿出整整一年呢？

w.m: phr. 暂时抽出整整一年

sentences.en: Well, everyone gets confused when you say gap year. They’re like, “What? It’s a whole year?” No, it’s not.
sentences.zh: 一说到间隔年，大家就容易误解。他们会说：“什么？是整整一年吗？”不，不是的。

w.m: phr. 感到困惑；产生误解

sentences.en: A gap year is just time-out between life stages.
sentences.zh: 间隔年只是人生两个阶段之间的一段暂歇。

sentences.en: People from all ages and all backgrounds take a gap year.
sentences.zh: 各个年龄、各种背景的人都可以过间隔年。

sentences.en: You know, and a majority of this time, I’d say it’s usually only for three to nine months?
sentences.zh: 而且，大多数时候，我想通常也就三到九个月。

sentences.en: Anyway, back to the question. If people only want to travel for a month or so, then there are a number of short gap options.
sentences.zh: 总之，回到刚才的问题。如果只想旅行一个月左右，也有很多短期的间隔年方案可选。

sentences.en: For example, they can travel around China or Southeast Asia, taking in the sights.
sentences.zh: 例如，可以环游中国或东南亚，欣赏各地风景。

sentences.en: They can volunteer in South America, and they can go on an overland tour in Africa.
sentences.zh: 可以去南美洲做志愿者，也可以在非洲进行陆路旅行。

sentences.en: There are endless opportunities out there.
sentences.zh: 机会多得数不清。

sentences.en: All you need to do is decide what it is you want to see and do.
sentences.zh: 你只需要决定自己想看什么、做什么。

sentences.en: Short gaps are like ultra-concentrated gap years.
sentences.zh: 短期间隔年就像高度浓缩版的间隔年。

sentences.en: Now, another question. You yourself travelled and volunteered in your gap year, so why is that a good option?
sentences.zh: 接下来还有一个问题。您在自己的间隔年中既旅行又做志愿者，为什么这是一个好选择？

sentences.en: Because you’re not only making a direct difference to local people’s lives, but you’re also learning more about specific culture and society.
sentences.zh: 因为你不仅直接改变了当地人的生活，也能更深入地了解某个地区特有的文化和社会。

sentences.en: Often, you can learn a lot more about an area volunteering than just travelling around.
sentences.zh: 通常，相比单纯四处旅行，做志愿者能让你对一个地方有更深入的了解。

sentences.en: We’d love to find out what is on people’s travel list. Could you tell us yours?
sentences.zh: 我们很想知道大家的旅行愿望清单上都有什么。您能说说自己的吗？

sentences.en: I think travel list has to be as ridiculous as possible.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，旅行愿望清单就应该尽可能天马行空。

w.m: adj. 荒诞的；异想天开的

sentences.en: It has to be made up of things that are achievable and things that are perhaps unachievable.
sentences.zh: 其中既要有能够实现的事情，也要有一些或许实现不了的事情。

sentences.en: After all, what do you do when you’ve done everything.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，如果所有事情都做完了，你接下来还能做什么呢？

sentences.en: Ah... on my travel list, number one, cage diving with great white sharks; number two, hitchhiking across America from New York to San Francisco; number three, touring overland in Africa, and number four is climbing Mount Qomolangma, which, let’s be honest, I need to think twice.
sentences.zh: 我的旅行清单上，第一项是在防护笼里潜水，近距离接触大白鲨；第二项是搭便车横穿美国，从纽约到旧金山；第三项是在非洲进行陆路旅行；第四项是攀登珠穆朗玛峰，不过说实话，这一项我得三思。

sentences.en: So, Jim, you’ve travelled a huge amount for somebody who is only 26 years old.
sentences.zh: 吉姆，您才26岁，却已经去过这么多地方了。

sentences.en: I’m curious, how did you get the travel bug?
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，您是怎么迷上旅行的？

sentences.en: Well, firstly, I grew up in an international household with a German mother and an Italian-American father, so our daily lives and conversations always were more global in a lot of ways.
sentences.zh: 首先，我在一个国际化家庭里长大，母亲是德国人，父亲是意大利裔美国人，因此我们的日常生活和交谈，在很多方面都更具全球视野。

w.m: adj. 意大利裔美国人的

sentences.en: Thus, I always saw the world as small and attainable.
sentences.zh: 所以，在我眼中，世界一直既小又触手可及。

w.m: adj. 可到达的；可实现的

sentences.en: Secondly, when I was 16, I left home to go to the United World College, which is a two-year boarding school with students from 90 different countries.
sentences.zh: 其次，16岁时，我离家去了世界联合学院；那是一所学制两年的寄宿学校，学生来自90个不同国家。

sentences.en: There, I really grew to see the entire world as an interconnected place, and began to think of myself less with national identities and more through global and human lenses.
sentences.zh: 在那里，我真正开始把整个世界看成相互联系的整体；我不再主要以国籍来定位自己，而是更多地从全球和人类整体的视角看待自己。

sentences.en: These two things really explain my love for the world and help to explain my love for travel, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想，这两件事确实能解释我为何热爱这个世界，也能解释我为何热爱旅行。

sentences.en: I see. And what will visiting every country in the world mean to you, personally?
sentences.zh: 我明白了。那么，对您个人来说，走遍世界上每一个国家意味着什么？

sentences.en: For me, it'll be about how much I’ve learned.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，关键是看自己学到了多少。

sentences.en: It will be a validation of my ability to think critically and analyze the different ways that societies try to function.
sentences.zh: 这会检验我能否批判性地思考，并分析不同社会努力运作的各种方式。

sentences.en: There’s so much to learn from personal experience or being in a place.
sentences.zh: 亲身经历或置身某地，都能让人学到很多东西。

sentences.en: And I love travel, because to me, it’s about constant learning.
sentences.zh: 我热爱旅行，因为对我而言，旅行意味着不断学习。

sentences.en: Yeah, “Travel broadens one’s mind,” as the saying goes.
sentences.zh: 正如那句俗话说的：“旅行开阔眼界。”

w.m: 谚语. 旅行开阔眼界

sentences.en: Well, Jim, thank you very much for joining us on the interview.
sentences.zh: 吉姆，非常感谢您参加我们的访谈。

w.m: phr. 参与某人的活动或节目

sentences.en: My pleasure.
sentences.zh: 我的荣幸。

w.m: 交际用语. 我的荣幸；不客气

sentences.en: What does the man say about a gap year?
sentences.zh: 这位男士对间隔年有什么看法？

sentences.en: According to the man, why is volunteering a good option?
sentences.zh: 根据这位男士的说法，为什么做志愿者是一个好选择？

sentences.en: Which of the following activities is the man least likely to do?
sentences.zh: 下列活动中，这位男士最不可能做的是哪一项？

sentences.en: What contributes to the man’s love for travelling?
sentences.zh: 是什么促成了这位男士对旅行的热爱？

sentences.en: What does the man see as a personal benefit of global travelling?
sentences.zh: 这位男士认为，环球旅行能给个人带来什么益处？

待核: 原PDF第5页主持人说“I see.”，OCR为“Oh, I see.”；最终应以原声核准是否有Oh，目前按扫描更正为I see。
